task_message:
Case M44: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 321x321x226 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Done. I segmented the myxoid soft-tissue tumor in the left lateral thigh/hip region on the T2-weighted volume.

**Approach**
- Scanned the volume with axial/coronal/sagittal contact sheets to localize the large, markedly T2-hyperintense, multilobulated mass.
- Seeded the model with a positive point in the bright core (v1), then a second positive point on the more heterogeneous posterior lobules (v2), which produced a single connected component of ~459 mL (axial 40–129, coronal 115–250, sagittal 45–145).
- Verified the boundary at the poles (ax 32/40/45/125/137, cor 107/125/250/258, sag 37/55/140/153) and at mid-levels (ax 60/62/73/84/105/115), checked with mask-fill overlays and zoomed views.
- Ran `fill_holes` (only +0.2 mL, confirming a solid mask) and reviewed the automatic candidates: C1 was a uniform ~3 mm shell (partial-volume/edema) and C2–C5 were tiny vessel-like structures, so all were rejected.

**Result:** single-component mask, 458.9 mL, following the entire bright lobulated mass including its less intense heterogeneous portions; confidence medium (some residual uncertainty about a thin hyperintense peritumoral rim and small satellite bright spots).
